item.title: European stock market open: Stocks push higher across the board but US tech woes linger
item.description:
European equities are enjoying a solid start to the session with major indices seen opening higher across the board. While regional stocks are holding up well, just be wary that the more cautious mood in US futures suggests that investors aren't quite ready to throw caution to the wind just yet. Here are the opening levels in Europe:

  • Eurostoxx +0.6%
  • Germany DAX +0.3%
  • France CAC 40 +1.2%
  • UK FTSE 100 +0.8%
  • Spain IBEX +1.3%
  • Italy FTSE MIB +0.4%

The positive start comes as European stocks are looking to build on yesterday's rebound, with buyers continuing to find some encouragement after the US midterm elections and the continued rotation out of tech shares.

In that lieu, the mood across the Atlantic is looking rather less optimistic. Dow futures may be up 0.5% but S&P 500 futures are trading flat while Nasdaq futures are down 0.7% so far today. That suggests the stunning recovery in tech shares yesterday may already be running out of steam.

And with AI spending concerns and the potential fallout from the US midterms still hanging over the tech sector, Wall Street could once again prove to be the bigger test for broader risk sentiment later today.

For now though, European investors are at least making the most of the calmer mood - even if the divergence with US tech stocks is still one to keep an eye out for.

As the week winds down, we will have the BOE policy decision coming up later before the weekly jobless claims data in the US. And finally tomorrow, we'll get to the main event this week as the US jobs report will come into focus and give markets some data direction to work with after the midterms.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: Gold's key breakout signals a potential trend reversal as Vance's comments fuel de-escalation bets
item.description:
Gold extended the gains yesterday after breaking above a key trendline that’s been defining the downtrend since September.

The breakout was driven by a selloff in oil prices after the US Vice President Vance blamed the war with Iran for the Republican Party's heavy losses in the midterm elections. His post published on X reinforced market expectations that the Trump administration could seek an off-ramp from the war rather than escalate military operations.

Keep in mind that a Democratic congress is also going to restrict further tax cuts, defence spending and fiscal expansion in general. And this is positive for gold because it’s going to limit the rise in Treasury yields and the US dollar on lower rate hike expectations.

It could also support gold in case Trump decides to escalate the war with Iran as inflation expectations would rise alongside weakening growth outlook given fiscal constraints, creating a stagflationary environment.

Tomorrow, we have the US NFP report, but the data is unlikely to change the Fed’s outlook much as the market got used to strong labour market data. The focus will likely remain on US-Iran negotiations, but at this point, it looks like both an escalation and a de-escalation would be bullish for gold.

 

GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see that gold(CFD contract) broke above the key downward trendline yesterday opening the door for a rally into the 4,700 level. The buyers will likely continue to pile in around these levels, with a defined risk below the trendline, to keep targeting new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will need to see the price breaking below the major upward trendline to open the door for new lows.

GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 4 hour chart, we have a minor support zone around the 4,080 level. If we get a pullback, we can expect the buyers to step in around the support, with a defined risk below the broken trendline, to keep pushing into new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price falling back below the trendline to position for a drop into the major upward trendline, targeting a breakout.

GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor upward trendline defining the bullish momentum on this timeframe. Aggressive buyers will likely lean on the trendline, with a defined risk below it, to keep pushing into new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break to extend the pullback into the 4,080 support, targeting a break below it. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

UPCOMING CATALYSTS

Todaywe get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. Tomorrow, we conclude the week with the US NFP report and the University of Michigan Consumer sentiment survey.

item.title: Gold price recovery gathers pace after US midterms but $4,200 remains a major hurdle
item.description:
It seems that gold is finally showing a bit of fighting spirit again this week. After the beating the precious metal has taken over the past two months, I would say that gold buyers have earned themselves a little reason to smile perhaps. That being said, they still have to address the question of whether is this the start of something bigger or just another recovery that will eventually run out of steam?

Gold prices are up over 6% so far this week, with the US midterm elections providing an added boost to the rebound. The Democrats' sweeping victory has weighed on the dollar and now Treasury yields, giving gold some much-needed breathing room.

In the bigger picture though, things remain fairly complicated with the tech shares still looking rather indecisive and that is impacting the broader market mood too. And not to mention the questions surrounding the US-Iran war, Washington's fiscal spending plans, and the outlook for the Fed as well.

But even if one can argue that the fundamental backdrop is looking more promising, I would argue that the technical picture still needs quite a bit of convincing.

Looking at the daily chart, gold has managed to climb back above the $4,000 mark after briefly slipping below that key psychological level at the end of last week and early this week. That is a positive first step but the recovery is now running into a more meaningful test closer to $4,200.

That is where the 100-day moving average (red line) comes into play at around $4,203, alongside the previous resistance region around $4,200-20 that has kept a lid on price action since October.

It would take a firm break above that region to give buyers more confidence in chasing an extended recovery towards $4,300 and then perhaps the 200-day moving average (blue line) at $4,468 currently. Otherwise, another rejection here could quickly put the $4,000 level back under scrutiny.

Looking to the weekly chart, at least things are seemingly more encouraging when you zoom out. Gold buyers have managed to defend the region around $3,900 to $4,000, with the 100-week moving average (red line) providing an important technical cushion - for now at least. So, that keeps the broader bullish structure from completely falling apart even after the sharp correction from the highs earlier this year.

To sum up, I would say gold bulls have definitely won themselves a bit of a reprieve this week. But if they want to turn this recovery into something more convincing, getting past $4,200 is the next order of business. Until then, this looks to be more of a promising bounce rather than any bullish breakout in the precious metal.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: Germany industrial orders rebound in September but manufacturing recovery remains fragile
item.description:
• Germany September industrial orders +4.4% vs +4.8% m/m expected
  • Prior -10.6%; revised to -10.1%
  • Germany September industrial orders +3.3% y/y
  • Prior +3.2% (revised)

The strong rebound in German manufacturing orders in September comes mainly from a notable recovery in the automotive industry. New orders there grew by 10.5% on the month, after new orders and production had been at a low level in the two preceding months due to production changeovers and factory shutdowns. That had been a bit of a drag on the monthly figure as seen with the gnarly estimate in August.

Besides that, the growth in mechanical engineering also had a positive impact on the overall figure in climbing by 8.3% in September. This increase was driven by a major order for the production of internal combustion engines and turbines. However, that is somewhat offset by new orders in other vehicle manufacturing (aircraft, ships, trains, military vehicles), which declined by 10.4% compared to the previous month.

If excluding large orders, new orders in the German industry were 5.1% higher in September than in the month before. In the less volatile three-month comparison, new orders in Q3 2026 were 0.2% higher overall than in Q2 2026; excluding large orders, they rose by 0.1%.

Overall, this signals that the German manufacturing sector is still somewhat holding up despite plenty of headwinds throughout the year so far. But with price pressures ramping up again heading into the final quarter of the year, the outlook will remain challenging especially if businesses and consumers taking a bigger hit amid stronger inflation and rising borrowing costs.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: US futures fall again as tech stocks stumble, can Wall Street pull off another comeback?
item.description:
Just when you think that the worst might be over, the market looks to be deciding to throw another tantrum. After yesterday's impressive comeback, tech stocks are once again starting to give investors another headache today.

S&P 500 futures are down 0.3% while Nasdaq futures are falling by 1.3%, as the optimism following the US midterm elections starts to wear thin again. So, are we going to see another déjà vu moment?

I wouldn't be quick to rule that out. After all, yesterday's early beatdown eventually gave way to a remarkable turnaround with the Nasdaq closing 1.4% higher. That being said, the only problem is that the underlying concerns surrounding the AI trade haven't really gone anywhere.

The Democratic sweep has raised prospects of tougher scrutiny on AI infrastructure and data centre expansion. So, that is also putting investors in a bit of an awkward position.

On the one hand, slower spending could ease concerns about excessive capex among big tech and the mounting credit risks behind the AI boom. But on the other hand, it also threatens the ambitious growth projections that have helped justify lofty tech valuations.

Talk about being caught between a rock and a hard place, eh?

And let's not forget about the bond market here. The flight towards Treasuries in recent weeks hasn't necessarily been a vote of confidence in the economy. I would argue that part of that demand reflects investors getting nervous about debt financing in the AI sector, where widening credit spreads are making borrowing more expensive even as Treasury yields fall.

Putting all of that together, it's hardly the kind of reassuring backdrop that tech investors would like.

To make things even more complicated, there's also a rather intriguing flip side to this whole situation. If markets eventually embrace more disciplined AI spending, stocks could find some relief. However, improving risk appetite could also unwind the rally in the bond market and risk sending yields higher again.

With how messy the market flows can be, as seen with how things are playing out above, who's to say we won't get another dramatic turnaround later today? However, it is best to be reminded of the fact that there is a difference between dip buyers coming in to rescue the market and investors genuinely regaining confidence in the AI trade.

For now, I think we're seeing something of an in between. And that's keeping markets guessing still this week, although traders and investors will have little choice but to sort their feet out soon enough especially with the US jobs report coming up tomorrow.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: Nasdaq Futures Analysis for Day Traders Today: Bears Take Control Below 28,270 as Semiconductor Weakness Returns

Nasdaq Futures tradeCompass Today: Bears Take Control Below 28,270 as Semiconductor Weakness Returns

Nasdaq-100 Futures (NQ) | November 5, 2026

tradeCompass directional score: -6 / +10 (Bearish)

The Nasdaq futures tradeCompass has activated its bearish threshold at 28,270, putting sellers in control for now. With NQ trading around 28,217 at the time of this analysis, the immediate focus is on downside targets, while a sustained recovery above 28,400 would be needed to activate the bullish scenario.

Qualcomm's dramatic reversal raises another warning for Nasdaq bulls

The correction in semiconductor stocks may not be over.

Yesterday, Qualcomm (QCOM) rallied more than 5% during regular trading, only to reverse sharply following its earnings announcement. Shares subsequently fell approximately 9%-10% from their earlier intraday highs in extended trading.

The company reported weakness in its smartphone chip business, adding to concerns about the semiconductor sector. Reuters reported that Qualcomm's handset revenue declined 26% year over year.

For Nasdaq traders, the important takeaway is that even strong intraday rallies can prove vulnerable when the underlying sector remains under pressure.

This brings us to today's Nasdaq futures tradeCompass.

Nasdaq futures bearish below 28,270

The bearish threshold for today is 28,270, and it has already been activated.

At the time of publication, NQ futures are trading around 28,217, meaning that sellers have already pushed prices beneath the bearish activation level.

However, that does not necessarily mean short sellers should chase the decline.

One area I would watch for a potential short entry is approximately 28,260-28,265, should price rebound toward that region and show renewed rejection.

This would give traders an opportunity to consider entering closer to the bearish threshold rather than selling after a substantial move lower. Naturally, such a retest is not guaranteed.

Bearish partial profit targets

For traders operating on the short side, the following levels are worth monitoring:

The first target at 28,202 is deliberately relatively close. It offers an early opportunity to take partial profits and reduce exposure.

For example, traders who entered short closer to 28,260 may consider taking some profit at 28,202 and moving their stop toward their entry price.

Others prefer to wait until the second target, 27,975, before moving their stop to breakeven.

That is an individual trade-management decision, but my preference is generally to reduce risk progressively, particularly when trading a volatile instrument such as Nasdaq futures.

If selling pressure continues, 27,907 becomes the third downside consideration, followed by the deeper objective at 27,609.

These are potential areas for taking profits, not promises that price will reach every target.

Nasdaq futures bullish above 28,400

Although the bears currently have the advantage, tradeCompass always provides an alternative scenario.

For today, 28,400 is the bullish activation threshold.

A move above that level, followed by sustained trading there, would indicate that buyers are recovering important territory.

Importantly, a brief spike above 28,400 would not necessarily be sufficient. I would want to see some evidence of acceptance above that area rather than another failed recovery.

Bullish partial profit targets

If the bullish threshold is activated, the following upside levels become relevant:

The first bullish target at 28,453 is relatively nearby and can serve a similar risk-reduction purpose to the first bearish target.

Beyond that, traders can monitor 28,489 and 28,569, followed by the higher objectives at 28,689 and 28,807, if the recovery develops further.

Notice that there are five bullish targets compared with four bearish targets. The distances between them are also quite different.

This is intentional.

Why tradeCompass profit targets are not evenly spaced

One important principle of tradeCompass is that markets do not move according to an evenly spaced ladder of profit targets.

Instead, I look at the market's existing structure, including historical price reactions, volume profiles, VWAP references, and areas where meaningful trading activity has previously occurred.

These help identify potential liquidity concentrations and areas where institutional participants or algorithmic strategies might react.

Sometimes two important levels are relatively close together. At other times, there can be a considerable distance between them.

This is why today's bullish and bearish target sequences have different spacing and different numbers of objectives.

The intention is not to predict the exact turning point of every move. It is to identify places where traders may want to pay closer attention, take partial profits, or reassess their positions.

What does today's Nasdaq tradeCompass mean for swing traders and dip buyers?

Although tradeCompass is primarily designed for day traders, I believe it can provide useful supporting information for traders operating over longer time horizons.

For swing traders, the bullish and bearish thresholds can help assess whether short-term momentum is improving or deteriorating.

For longer-term investors, the same information can provide some perspective when considering buying market pullbacks.

For example, a long-term investor may have already decided that a particular Nasdaq stock represents attractive value following a correction.

That is a fundamentally different decision from an intraday futures trade.

Nevertheless, when tradeCompass has already activated its bearish threshold, as it has today, I would not regard that as the ideal technical environment for rushing to buy the dip.

It may be more sensible to observe whether selling pressure starts to stabilize, or whether buyers can eventually reclaim important technical levels.

Of course, a long-term investment thesis should not be determined by a single intraday trading indicator.

How to approach today's Nasdaq futures market

My preference today is to respect the activated bearish scenario rather than anticipate a bullish reversal before the evidence appears.

The key levels are straightforward:

Below 28,270: The bearish scenario remains active, with 28,202 as the first downside objective and 27,975 as the next substantial target.

Near 28,260-28,265: A potential retest area where short sellers may look for renewed weakness, rather than automatically entering without confirmation.

Above 28,400: The bullish scenario becomes relevant, provided price can sustain the recovery.

The other important consideration is patience.

TradeCompass is a decision-support framework, not an invitation to trade every price movement. There is no need to overtrade, and sometimes the better decision is simply to wait for price to reach an area of interest.

After the first or second partial profit target is reached, traders should seriously consider reducing exposure or moving their stop toward breakeven, while accounting for execution costs and the possibility of slippage.

Bottom line: Nasdaq futures remain bearish according to today's tradeCompass. The burden is on buyers to reclaim 28,400 before the technical picture improves meaningfully.

item.title: Oil prices plunge after US midterms as WTI crude faces a critical technical test
item.description:
Apparently, the quickest way to bring oil prices back down is to give Trump a good old-fashioned electoral beating. That seems to be what the market is telling us after the Democrats swept the US midterms at least.

WTI crude is coming under heavy selling pressure since overnight as traders are betting that Trump's political setback could pave the way for a de-escalation of the US-Iran war. So, why exactly the change of heart?

Well, Trump now faces a much tougher political landscape at home after Democrats have taken over control of Congress. The war has already taken a toll on the average American through higher energy prices and the election results suggest that voters have had enough. So, the idea here is perhaps that might finally give Washington a stronger incentive to pursue diplomacy rather than further escalation.

That being said, are oil traders getting a little ahead of themselves here?

We've seen time and time again that hopes for peace are one thing, but actually getting a deal across the finish line is a whole other thing. And while there is hopeful optimism among traders again now, there's still no guarantee that either Washington or Tehran will make the necessary concessions needed to end the conflict.

As for oil prices, we're now approaching a crossroads of sorts this week.

WTI crude is testing a critical support region around $86.80 to $87.00, where the 100-day (red line) and 200-day (blue line) moving averages are converging. The 50.0 Fib retracement level of the rally from July to September also sits nearby at $86.90, adding to the significance of this price region.

But at least for now, sellers are looking poised after already forcing a break below the trendline support from the July to August lows. As such, that leaves buyers with an important defensive job on their hands.

A firm daily close below this support region could invite a deeper correction towards the 61.8 Fibi retracement level at $82.21, before the psychological $80 mark comes into focus.

Conversely, buyers will need to reclaim a break above the swing region around $88.75 to $88.00 to wrestle back some control and then $95 again to begin repairing the technical damage.

On the balance of things, I'd argue that the technical picture is starting to favour sellers at the moment. But with the Iran war still unresolved, one unexpected headline could easily turn this latest selloff on its head.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

Summary:

  • AI and chip stocks extended their slide across Asia, with the Kospi down about 4.8% after a sidecar halted program trading, and the Nikkei down about 1.5%
  • The broader Topix rose about 1.4%, while China’s Shanghai Composite jumped about 3.6% and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng about 3%
  • SoftBank fell almost 6%, hit by Arm’s slide, the AI selloff and an FT report that China has blocked its $5.4 billion ABB robotics deal
  • Oil stayed lower on hopes of US-Iran diplomacy, though the IRGC claimed fresh tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz
  • Gold extended Wednesday’s 3% jump to around $4,135
  • BoJ minutes showed the board backing further hikes; the Bank of England is expected to raise rates to 4% at 12:00 GMT

Equities

Asian markets split sharply on Thursday as the rotation out of AI and chip stocks that began on Wall Street overnight deepened, while most other sectors rallied on lower oil prices after Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections.

Korea bore the brunt. The Kospi slumped about 4.8% and the Kosdaq about 4.3%, with the selling heavy enough to trigger a sidecar, a five-minute pause in program trading tied to sharp moves in KOSPI 200 futures. The exchange also said trading will open an hour late on November 19 to keep roads clear for the national university entrance exam.

In Tokyo, the market divided along the same line. The broad Topix rose about 1.4%, led by real estate, retail and pharmaceuticals, while the tech-heavy Nikkei fell about 1.5% as chip equipment makers Advantest and Tokyo Electron slumped. Most Nikkei members rose, but losses in a handful of heavily weighted tech stocks dragged the index lower. Sony and Nintendo report after the close.

SoftBank Group fell about 5.8% to around ¥4,020. It was already down about 5% in the morning, weighed by a post-results slide in its chip designer Arm and the AI selloff, before the Financial Times reported during the lunch break that Chinese regulators had told the company they would not allow its $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB’s robotics division. China’s National Development and Reform Commission informed SoftBank of the decision, according to the report, and SoftBank is assessing whether it can seek approval again.

Chinese markets moved the other way. The Shanghai Composite jumped about 3.6% and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng about 3%.

US equity index futures were around 7,705 for the S&P 500 and 28,271 for the Nasdaq 100.

Oil and the Strait of Hormuz

Oil prices stayed lower, with Brent around $97 a barrel and WTI around $88, as the midterm result raised hopes of a diplomatic path with Iran. President Trump said the US had no immediate plans for military action, and Qatar stepped up mediation, though an Iranian official said the two sides remain far from agreement.

Late in the session, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed that two tankers and a tugboat had caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and separately said a tanker using what it called an unapproved route had struck a mine. The claims could not be independently verified. They follow a series of similar IRGC claims in recent weeks and are a reminder of the risk to the diplomacy-driven fall in oil.

In a separate report, Bloomberg said Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. was considering a third pipeline to bypass Hormuz that could be opened to other producers. ADNOC called the report inaccurate and purely speculative.

Gold

Gold extended its rally to around $4,135 an ounce, building on Wednesday’s jump of about 3%, its biggest daily gain since August. The move has come alongside lower oil, a weaker dollar and softer Treasury yields, rather than rising tensions. That fits a case set out by Citi, which argues that a sustained fall in oil could shift the Federal Reserve from hiking to cutting and revive gold’s rally, with targets of $4,500 over three months and $5,000 over six to 12 months. Fed futures still price a high chance of a December hike, however.

Central banks

Minutes of the Bank of Japan’s September meeting, when it raised rates to 1.25% in a 7-2 vote, showed members agreed to keep lifting rates. One said the pace may need to accelerate if prices overshoot, while members flagged a roughly 50% rise in crude since July as a key inflation risk. The government’s representative urged the bank to weigh the cumulative effect of past hikes. A private survey showed Japan’s services sector expanded slightly faster in October, though hiring slowed and cost pressures stayed sharp.

Swiss National Bank Chairman Martin Schlegel said October’s 1.5% inflation rate surprised the central bank and that it would not hesitate to adjust policy if needed, adding to expectations of a December hike.

The Bank of England is widely expected to raise Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4% at 12:00 GMT (07:00 ET), its first hike of this cycle, with guidance on further moves and new inflation forecasts in focus.

Currencies

USD/JPY was around 157.80, AUD/USD around 0.7013 and EUR/USD around 1.1263. Australia’s goods trade surplus widened to about A$2.8 billion in September, a seven-month high, on stronger LNG and metals exports and a sharp drop in gold imports.

Also in focus

AstraZeneca has made an offer of around $10 billion for obesity drugmaker Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, The Wall Street Journal reported, sending Rhythm shares up 28%.

Goldman Sachs estimates that states likely to tighten rules on data centres hold about 45% of planned US capacity, though it expects any pauses to be short-lived. UBS raised its AI capital spending forecasts, while Citrini Research said growth in AI infrastructure investment has peaked.

In US earnings, Qualcomm beat forecasts but slipped on softer profit guidance, while Snap beat on profit but missed on users.

item.title: Bitcoin analysis after the US midterms: Bulls are back, but $82,000 could change everything
item.description:
Bitcoin price analysis: Sellers failed below $76,000. Now buyers face $81,460

Bitcoin CME futures swept to $75,795 and rebounded on unusually heavy trading. The four-hour recovery is encouraging, but holding $79,040 and clearing $81,460 would tell us much more about whether buyers have genuinely regained control.

Bitcoin CME futures have changed character in the space of a few sessions. After aggressive selling and repeated attempts to extend the decline, the market briefly broke below $76,000, recovered, and then rallied to $81,460 on November 4. It is a promising short-term reversal attempt, but the difference between a rebound and a lasting change of trend still matters.

The starting point is straightforward: sellers achieved a fresh low but could not sustain the breakdown. Buyers then produced a much more decisive upward move. That echoes the lesson in Greg Michalowski's earlier Bitcoin analysis of sellers failing to extend a support break. His article examines different Bitcoin price references, so the levels in this CME futures analysis should be evaluated on their own terms.

How Bitcoin went from heavy selling to a possible reversal

October 29: Sellers set the tone. CME Bitcoin futures traded as high as $82,270 before reversing. One four-hour candle fell from an $81,525 open to a $79,045 close. Another ended at $77,025 on volume of 4,141 contracts. There was no need to guess who had the advantage then: the price was moving substantially lower.

October 30: Trading activity remained intense, but downside progress became less convincing. A four-hour candle traded between $76,550 and $78,200 on 4,576 contracts, yet opened at $77,425 and closed at $77,420, a net loss of just $5. That does not prove buyers were accumulating Bitcoin. It does show a great deal of trading without a meaningful change between the open and close.

November 3: The break below the lows failed. A later four-hour candle fell to $75,795, undercutting earlier lows around $76,260-$76,450, then closed back at $77,905. This could have been a liquidity sweep, when a price move through a well-watched low triggers orders but fails to establish a new lower trading range. We can see the failed break in the price data; we cannot independently verify the stop orders or intentions behind it.

November 4: Buyers finally generated meaningful upward displacement. A four-hour candle opened at $78,535, climbed to $81,460 and closed at $80,655, with volume of 5,468 contracts. That was about 5.1 times the preceding 20-bar average of 1,066 contracts. The comparison is striking, although the average includes thinly traded periods around the weekend, so the multiple should not be treated as a calibrated signal.

By the last completed four-hour bar in the supplied November 5 snapshot, futures had closed at $80,925. The following bar was still developing. These are dated CME continuous-futures observations, not a live Bitcoin spot quote.

The lesson in volume: Effort is useful, but the result matters more

Volume measures how much trading took place. It does not, by itself, tell us which side is winning.

Compare the two unusually active four-hour candles. On October 30, 4,576 contracts accompanied a candle body of minus $5. On November 4, 5,468 contracts accompanied a candle body of plus $2,120. There was plenty of activity on both occasions, but only the second produced a decisive net change in price.

The first pattern is consistent with buyers meeting aggressive selling or with two-sided trading. The second is stronger evidence that buyers were able to push prices higher. Neither observation proves institutional accumulation, trapped short positions or a particular order-flow mechanism. Four-hour open, high, low, close and volume data simply cannot settle those questions.

This is why the sequence matters more than an isolated green candle. Heavy selling met limited progress near the lows, a lower break failed, and a subsequent high-volume rally reclaimed resistance. For the November 5 snapshot, that supports a short-term directional assessment of +6 on a -10 to +10 scale. It is a conditional assessment, not a 60% probability, validated trading signal or promise of further upside.

$79,040 is the pivot. $81,460 is the next hurdle.

The $79,040 region repeatedly interrupted recovery attempts before November 4. The bullish move carried futures back above it. That makes the former resistance area particularly informative on any pullback.

A breakout is not the same as a successful retest. Price can rise through a ceiling and immediately fall back below it. A more convincing transition occurs when buyers defend the old ceiling as a new floor, or when price builds acceptance above it without needing a deep pullback.

The first nearer-term potential support zone is $80,160-$80,465, drawn from the post-breakout price action. Below it, $79,040 is the more important structural pivot. Overhead, $81,460 is the breakout-session high, followed by the earlier $82,270 high. Reaching a level is not the same as holding beyond it.

Why the macro backdrop can help, or interrupt, this Bitcoin recovery

The chart gives us a price-based argument, not a complete explanation of why Bitcoin moved. Other markets were also repricing political and economic risks following the US midterm elections.

In commodities, oil prices dropped sharply as markets priced hopes of an end to the Iran war. That is a market expectation, not evidence that a diplomatic deal has been completed. Gold's rise alongside falling oil and a weaker dollar offers another useful piece of context: lower energy prices can reduce inflation pressure, but the interest-rate response and the durability of diplomacy remain uncertain.

Inside crypto, the November 3 Ethereum outlook emphasized the difficult pre-election and geopolitical backdrop. A November 4 analysis of Zcash's rebound explored the possible influence of falling Treasury yields and a weaker dollar, while also flagging coin-specific factors. Together, these reports suggest that crypto's recovery deserves to be tested against the dollar, yields and broader risk appetite rather than attributed only to technical levels.

Yet this is not a uniformly bullish backdrop for all risk assets. The market's positive response to the prospect of slower hyperscaler data-center spending shows that investors can reward some large technology companies while turning away from parts of the AI infrastructure trade. Bitcoin may benefit from improved financial conditions without every equity segment rising alongside it.

Three Bitcoin scenarios worth watching

1. Bullish continuation: Buyers clear $81,460. A completed four-hour close above $81,460, followed by sustained trading above it, would make $82,270 the next upside reference. Acceptance above $82,270 would offer stronger evidence of structural recovery. A brief intrabar spike through either level, followed by rejection, would be less persuasive.

2. Constructive consolidation: Buyers defend the breakout. A pullback toward $80,160-$80,465, or even toward $79,040, would not automatically destroy the bullish case. What matters is whether selling loses momentum and buyers can establish support. A successful defense would improve the quality of the recovery, even without an immediate new high. A pullback is a possibility, not a forecast that orders placed there will fill.

3. Failed breakout: Price loses $79,040. A decisive four-hour move back below that pivot, especially if a recovery attempt fails and downside volume expands, would undermine the short-term bullish assessment. The next historical reference is around $77,417, followed by the $75,795 reversal low. A sustained move beneath the latter would seriously challenge the idea that the November 3 break was a durable bottom.

When might waiting be more useful than trading? If Bitcoin remains between nearby support and $81,460 without decisive follow-through, the reward for guessing the next move may be limited. More informative observations would include a completed breakout close, a well-defended pullback, or a clear failed reclaim of $79,040. Those are conditions to evaluate, not mandatory entries or a complete trade plan.

The takeaway: A failed breakdown is an opening, not a guarantee

The Bitcoin futures recovery deserves attention because sellers pushed below prior lows but could not maintain control, and buyers answered with a strong, high-volume move. The important next question is whether Bitcoin can hold the ground it recovered and move above $81,460-$82,270. If it cannot, the rally may remain only a temporary repair within a fragile broader market.

The wider-market lesson also matters. In September 1 trading in Japan, 168 of the Nikkei's 225 stocks were rising at one point even as the index slipped and the broader Topix gained. Influential AI names were weighing on the Nikkei despite wider participation elsewhere. A headline index can conceal mixed underlying behavior, just as a Bitcoin rebound can conceal unresolved resistance. Watch what actually advances, what fails to follow through, and whether the market confirms its first move.

The next chapter for Bitcoin is not settled by one bullish candle. The response to $79,040 on weakness and $81,460 on strength is likely to be more informative than a prediction made in advance.

Bitcoin's $82,000 price magnet: Why reaching the level is only half the story

Bitcoin's strong rebound from around $76,000 has brought an interesting question into focus: Could $82,000 become the next destination for buyers?

In my view, the $82,000 area is becoming increasingly interesting, not because Bitcoin is guaranteed to reach it, but because several historical price references cluster around $81,900-$82,000.

In trading, we sometimes call this a price magnet. Think of it as an area where buyers and sellers may have unfinished business. Previous trading activity can make certain prices particularly interesting, attracting traders looking to enter, exit or take profits.

But here's an important lesson: A price magnet is not necessarily a level that price will break through.

What should Bitcoin traders watch?

The November 4 BTCUSD chart analysis identified several useful areas to monitor:

First, $80,750-$80,900. If Bitcoin can climb through this area and remain above it, that would strengthen the case for another advance. A brief jump above resistance is less convincing than price staying there.

Next, $81,850-$81,975. This is the main area of interest around the $82,000 price magnet. Traders who bought earlier may consider taking profits, while other participants may be preparing for a breakout.

Above $82,050-$82,150. If Bitcoin moves beyond $82,000 and continues trading above this area, it would provide more convincing evidence that buyers are maintaining control.

And what if Bitcoin starts falling instead? Holding $80,000-$80,150 would help preserve the recovery. A sustained decline below $79,900 would make me more cautious, with $79,122 becoming another downside reference.

These levels come from a November 4 BTCUSD chart snapshot. They are not live prices or interchangeable with CME Bitcoin futures execution levels.

Three things can happen when Bitcoin approaches $82,000

1. Bitcoin breaks through. Buyers push above $82,000, and price continues trading there. Traders call this price acceptance. It suggests the market is becoming comfortable at higher prices.

2. Bitcoin breaks through, then reverses. Price briefly rises above $82,000 but falls back below it. This may happen as breakout orders are triggered and sellers respond. It can look bullish initially but turn into a failed breakout.

3. Bitcoin never quite reaches $82,000. Some traders may take profits before the expected resistance, causing the rally to lose momentum. A price magnet can attract interest without ever being touched.

Why patience may be the better opportunity

I am less interested in chasing Bitcoin after its sharp recovery and more interested in watching how the market behaves as it approaches $82,000.

For traders already holding a profitable position, approaching an important resistance area may be an opportunity to consider partial profits or reduce risk. For those looking for a new entry, waiting for a confirmed breakout or a successful pullback may provide more useful information than buying simply because the price is rising.

The broader lesson applies far beyond Bitcoin: Predicting where price might go is only one part of trading. Understanding how price behaves when it gets there can be even more valuable.

The destination is interesting. The reaction at the destination may be even more important.

Educational only. Trade at your own risk.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: China blocks SoftBank’s $5.4 billion ABB robotics deal, FT says, in blow to Son’s AI push
item.description:
The block adds a regulatory overhang to SoftBank on a day the shares were already under pressure from Arm and the AI selloff, and uncertainty over whether a fresh application is viable may keep that pressure on. For ABB, the robotics unit stays on its books, with investors likely to focus on whether it revives a separation plan. China’s role as the largest market for the business gives Beijing significant leverage, a reminder of the late-stage risk Chinese reviews pose to cross-border tech deals. Robotics and automation names may see sentiment effects as the physical AI investment case faces a geopolitical hurdle.

- Son wanted ABB’s robots for SoftBank’s physical AI future; the robots’ biggest market has said no.

Summary:

  • Chinese regulators told SoftBank they will not allow its $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB’s robotics division, the FT reported
  • SoftBank was informed by China’s National Development and Reform Commission, according to the report
  • SoftBank is assessing what went wrong and whether it can reapply
  • China is the biggest market for ABB’s robotics unit
  • The deal had won unconditional EU approval in March
  • SoftBank shares fell about 5%, also hit by Arm’s slide and the AI selloff

Chinese regulators have told SoftBank Group they will not allow its $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB’s robotics division, the Financial Times reported on Thursday, citing multiple people familiar with the matter, dealing a setback to Chief Executive Masayoshi Son’s push into what he calls physical AI.

According to the report, as relayed by Investing.com, SoftBank was informed of the decision by China’s National Development and Reform Commission, the country’s top economic planning agency. SoftBank is now trying to establish what went wrong and whether it can seek approval again, the FT said. The grounds for the decision were not disclosed.

China’s stance carries particular weight because it is the largest market for ABB’s robotics unit.

SoftBank agreed in October 2025 to buy 100% of the Swiss engineering group’s robotics business for about $5.375 billion, with completion planned for mid-to-late 2026. The European Commission cleared the deal without conditions in March, while approvals from China and the United States were still pending as of late October.

The unit generated about $2.3 billion in revenue in 2024, roughly 7% of ABB’s group total, and employs around 7,000 people. Son had made robotics a major part of SoftBank’s AI strategy, describing physical AI, the combination of artificial intelligence with machines that act in the real world, as the group’s next frontier.

The news will compound a difficult session for SoftBank, whose shares fell about 5% in Tokyo morning trade (the exchange is closed for the lunch brak as this news crosses) , lagging a 0.5% decline in the Nikkei 225. The stock was weighed by an overnight slide in Arm Holdings, its prized chip designer, after Arm’s guidance for the current quarter underwhelmed, and by a broader selloff in AI-linked stocks after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterms. SoftBank’s large investment in OpenAI gives it significant exposure to the US data centre buildout that Democrats have signalled they will scrutinise more closely.

The next steps will be responses from SoftBank and ABB, and whether a renewed application or remedies can rescue the deal. If not, ABB will need to decide how it handles the robotics business on its own.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: 168 of 225 Nikkei stocks rise, but AI losses drag the index lower as the Topix rallies
item.description:
The Nikkei-Topix gap is likely to stay in focus as long as the rotation out of AI persists, with price-weighted chip heavyweights able to sink the Nikkei on a broadly positive day. Lower oil is a direct support for Japan’s terms of trade, favouring importers and domestic sectors over energy-sensitive shippers. Afternoon results from Toyota, and from Sony and Nintendo after the close, could test whether the rally broadens further. Any rebound in crude on setbacks in Iran talks would remove the main pillar under the move.

---

Earlier:

  • SoftBank faces two hits as Arm slide meets US rotation out of AI, leaving Nikkei exposed

---

Most of Japan’s market cheered cheaper oil; the handful of AI giants that move the Nikkei did not.

Summary:

  • The Topix rose about 1.3% in early trade while the Nikkei slipped 0.5%
  • 168 of the Nikkei’s 225 stocks rose, but heavyweight tech losses dragged the index lower
  • Lower oil on hopes of an end to the Iran war lifted import-dependent Japan
  • Advantest fell about 10%, Tokyo Electron about 9% and SoftBank Group around 5%
  • Real estate, retail and pharma led; shipping was the weakest sector

Japanese stocks rallied broadly on Thursday as lower oil prices lifted most of the market, but a deepening selloff in AI and chip shares left the Nikkei 225 in the red, with SoftBank Group among the heaviest drags, Reuters reported.

The broader Topix rose 1.3% in early trade, after gaining as much as 2.4%, while the Nikkei slipped 0.5%. The split was stark: 168 of the Nikkei’s 225 members were higher, but losses in a handful of heavily weighted tech names outweighed them.

The rally was driven by oil. Crude fell sharply after Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections, raising hopes for an end to the Iran war. Cheaper energy is a clear positive for Japan, which imports almost all of its energy needs, mostly from the Middle East.

AI-linked stocks went the other way, extending Wednesday’s losses on expectations that Democratic gains will slow the pace of US data centre expansion. Chip equipment makers Advantest and Tokyo Electron fell about 10% and 9% respectively, and SoftBank Group dropped around 5%, also weighed by a post-results slide in its chip designer Arm. One strategist said money that had flowed into AI and semiconductors was moving into other sectors, though he did not expect US-China competition to allow the data centre buildout to reverse.

Investors rotated into domestically focused and defensive sectors. Real estate led with a gain of about 6.5%, followed by retail and pharmaceuticals, with Uniqlo owner Fast Retailing up about 8%. Toyota rose ahead of its results, while Sony and Nintendo also gained before their earnings after the close. Shipping was the weakest sector on prospects of lower freight rates if the Middle East conflict eases.

The session played out much as flagged in this morning’s preview: a broadly firmer Japanese market, held back in the Nikkei by its reliance on AI-linked heavyweights.

item.title: Gold jumps as oil slumps on Iran diplomacy hopes, an early test of Citi’s thesis
item.description:
Oil is now the lead indicator for gold, with any further slide in crude likely to extend bullion’s gains through softer inflation expectations and a weaker dollar. The gap between that move and still-firm Fed hike pricing is the key tension: if rate markets start to follow oil lower, gold has room to run, but if they hold, the rally may stall. For energy traders, a 9% drop in Brent on diplomacy hopes alone shows how much risk premium remains in the price, and how quickly it could return if talks falter. The dollar’s slide adds a second tailwind for gold that may persist if US political uncertainty weighs on the currency.

Newswire cut: Gold rose about 3.3% to around $4,060, its biggest daily gain since August, as Brent fell about 9% on hopes of Iran diplomacy after the US midterms, in line with Citi’s view that de-escalation, not escalation, is what drives bullion higher

One-line wrap: Gold finally got the oil slump Citi said it needed, but the Fed has not yet played its part.

Summary:

  • Spot gold rose about 3.3% to around $4,060 an ounce, its biggest daily gain since August
  • Brent fell about 9% to roughly $94.50, its lowest since early September, on hopes of Iran diplomacy
  • The dollar fell to a one-month-plus low and Treasury yields eased after Democrats won Congress
  • Citi’s Max Layton has argued lower oil could flip the Fed to cuts and revive gold’s rally, with targets of $4,500 and $5,000
  • Markets still price about an 83% chance of a December Fed hike, per CME FedWatch
  • US payrolls and Iran talks are the next tests

Gold posted its strongest daily gain since August on Wednesday as oil prices slumped on hopes of a diplomatic path on Iran, offering an early test of Citi’s view that de-escalation, rather than escalation, is what bullion needs to rally.

Spot gold rose about 3.3% to around $4,060 an ounce, recovering further from a low near $3,870 on October 30. The move came as Brent crude fell about 9% to roughly $94.50 a barrel, its lowest since early September, and US crude dropped to around $88. The dollar slid to its weakest level in more than a month and Treasury yields eased. Gold up and oil down is continuing in Asia trade. 

The shift followed Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections, a result that raised hopes for a diplomatic approach to the conflict with Iran. President Trump said the US had no immediate plans for military action, and Qatar stepped up mediation efforts. An Iranian official cautioned, however, that Tehran and Washington remained far from an agreement.

The pattern matters because of how gold has traded through the war. Rather than rallying as a haven, it has tended to fall when tensions rose, as higher oil prices fed inflation fears and kept the Federal Reserve leaning toward tighter policy. Wednesday’s session ran that chain in reverse: lower oil, a weaker dollar and softer yields all supported bullion.

That is the scenario Citi set out in a recent note. Max Layton, the bank’s global head of commodities research, said much lower oil prices could prompt the Fed to shift from hiking to cutting rates, lifting investment demand for gold and reviving a momentum-driven rally. Citi has set a 0-3 month target of $4,500 an ounce and a 6-12 month target of $5,000, assuming the Strait of Hormuz reopens and the conflict de-escalates by year-end.

The Fed side of that equation has not moved yet. Futures markets were still pricing a high probability of a December rate hike, with CME’s FedWatch tool showing about 83%. Without a change in that outlook, the rally rests on lower oil and a softer dollar rather than an actual shift in policy expectations.

US payrolls data are the next test, alongside any concrete progress in talks with Iran. A durable fall in oil that begins to pull Fed pricing lower would strengthen the case Citi is making; a renewed flare-up in the region would likely reverse it. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Sidecars and exam days: two Korean market quirks explained as the KOSPI slides 4%
item.description:
A sidecar on a 4% down day signals forced or automated selling at pace, and traders will watch whether the pause steadies futures or merely delays further losses. Korea’s heavy weighting in chipmakers leaves it exposed to any extension of the overnight rotation out of AI-linked stocks, with knock-on effects for regional tech and the won. A weaker won could add to the pressure if foreign investors keep selling.

The November 19 timetable is a minor liquidity consideration, but one that can catch out overseas desks used to the normal opening time.

---

Korea hit the brakes on its trading algorithms today, and in two weeks it will hit pause for its students.

Summary:

  • The KOSPI fell around 4% on Thursday, and a sidecar briefly suspended program trading tied to KOSPI 200 futures
  • A sidecar halts program orders for five minutes when futures move sharply and stay there for a minute; normal trading continues
  • The slide coincided with an overnight selloff in AI and chip stocks on Wall Street
  • On November 19, KOSPI and KOSDAQ trading will open at 10:00 local time (01:00 GMT) and close at 16:30 (07:30 GMT), an hour later than usual
  • The delay is for the Suneung university entrance exam, when offices start late, flights pause and police help students reach exam halls

South Korea’s stock market offered a crash course in two of its more unusual mechanisms on Thursday. As the KOSPI slid around 4%, a “sidecar” briefly paused automated trading, while the exchange announced it will open an hour late later this month so students can get to their university entrance exams on time.

The sidecar came first. It is a circuit breaker for program trading: when KOSPI 200 futures move sharply against the previous close and stay there for a minute, the exchange suspends computer-driven program orders for five minutes. On the main board the trigger is a 5% move. Ordinary trading continues, but the pause is designed to stop automated selling or buying from feeding on itself during a fast market. A sidecar can only be triggered once a day.

Thursday’s slide coincided with a sharp selloff in AI and chip stocks on Wall Street overnight, a theme that weighs heavily on Korea given the index’s exposure to semiconductor makers.

The second quirk is gentler. The Korea Exchange said trading on the KOSPI and KOSDAQ will start at 10:00 local time on November 19 (01:00 GMT, or 20:00 ET on November 18), an hour later than usual, and close at 16:30 (07:30 GMT, 02:30 ET). After-hours trading will also shift an hour later, running from 17:00 to 20:00.

The reason is the Suneung, the national university entrance exam, which is treated as close to a national event. Results play a major role in which universities students can enter, and with around half a million candidates sitting it each year, the country rearranges itself around the day. Government offices and many companies delay their start times to keep roads clear, aircraft take-offs and landings are typically halted during the English listening section, and police stand by to rush late students to exam halls.

For investors trading Korea from overseas, both are worth knowing. A sidecar is a signal that futures are moving fast, while the exam-day timetable shifts when Korean price action feeds into the rest of the Asian session. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Bank of England preview: first hike to 4% expected as energy pushes inflation to 3.5%
item.description:
With a hike almost fully priced, sterling’s reaction will hinge on the vote split and guidance, with a 7-2 outcome and cautious language the most likely route to a softer pound. Gilts could rally if the Bank pushes back on market pricing for several more hikes, particularly at the short end. Oil is the swing factor beyond today: renewed strength in crude and gas would keep pressure on the Bank to tighten further, while any easing in Middle East tensions would weaken the case for a second move. The updated inflation projections will be scrutinised for how much of the energy shock the Bank expects to persist into 2027.

-

The Bank of England is set to hike; what it says about the next one will matter more.

Summary:

  • The BoE is widely expected to lift Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4%, at 12:00 GMT (07:00 ET)
  • It held at 3.75% in September in a 6-3 vote, with three members favouring a hike
  • UK CPI rose to 3.5% in September from 3.1%, driven by fuel costs
  • Goldman Sachs expects a 7-2 vote, with the committee ready to respond but giving no strong steer
  • Many economists see one more hike, to 4.25%, early next year, less than markets price
  • New forecasts are likely to show inflation peaking above 4% in early 2027

The Bank of England is widely expected to raise interest rates on Thursday for the first time in this cycle, lifting Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4% as energy costs push UK inflation further above target, with the decision due at 12:00 GMT (07:00 ET).

The move would follow a closely divided September meeting, when the Monetary Policy Committee held Bank Rate at 3.75% in a 6-3 vote, with three members already favouring a rise to 4%. Since then, the inflation picture has deteriorated. Consumer prices rose 3.5% in the year to September, up from 3.1% in August and higher than expected, driven largely by rising fuel costs.

Markets have almost fully priced in a hike, and research houses are close to unanimous. Goldman Sachs expects a 7-2 vote in favour, a split shared by much of the consensus, with the two likely dissenters preferring to hold. Some forecasters see a narrower margin.

The more important question for markets is what comes next. Money markets have priced in several further increases over the coming year, a path many economists consider too aggressive. The more common base case is one additional quarter-point rise early next year, taking Bank Rate to 4.25%, possibly in February, when inflation is projected to peak. Goldman expects the committee to signal readiness to respond if inflation pressure builds, but without a strong steer on future meetings.

This is also a forecast meeting, with the Bank publishing an updated Monetary Policy Report. Its new projections are likely to show a higher near-term inflation peak in the first half of 2027, with Goldman expecting it at above 4%. Oil and gas prices are now running above the adverse scenario the Bank set out in July, raising the risk that the Middle East conflict leaves a more lasting mark on UK inflation.

That is the central concern for the hawks. Underlying measures remain firm, with services inflation approaching 4%, and the key risk is that higher energy costs become embedded in wages and price-setting. Against that, wage growth has been described as soft and the consumer is under pressure, giving the doves grounds for caution.

For sterling and gilts, the guidance and vote split are likely to matter more than the hike itself. A cautious message alongside a widely expected increase could see markets pare back their more aggressive pricing, while any sign of a faster pace would reinforce it. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Berkshire adds $27 million of Sirius XM as investors rotate from AI toward value stocks
item.description:
A Berkshire purchase tends to act as a sentiment signal for the target stock, which may help sustain Sirius XM’s rally as long as the broader rotation holds. More widely, it adds a high-profile example to the case for cash-generative, buyback-heavy companies at a time when investors are questioning returns on AI spending. Other mature media and consumer names with strong free cash flow could draw interest on the same logic. If AI stocks rebound quickly, though, the appetite for value plays may fade as fast as it arrived.

--- While the market argues over AI spending, Berkshire is quietly buying a company that hands cash back to shareholders.

Summary:

  • Berkshire bought about 924,000 Sirius XM shares for roughly $27 million from October 30 to November 3, per a regulatory filing
  • Its stake is now about 125.7 million shares, roughly 37% of the company, held mainly through GEICO
  • It paid about $29 to $30 a share, versus about $21 to $22 in mid-2025
  • The buying followed Q3 results in which Sirius XM raised full-year guidance and flagged faster buybacks in 2027
  • It coincides with a broad rotation out of AI infrastructure stocks, though the purchases predate Wednesday’s selloff

Berkshire Hathaway has added to its stake in Sirius XM, buying about $27 million of shares over three trading days, a modest purchase for the conglomerate but one that lines up with a broader shift in investor appetite toward cash-generating, value-oriented stocks.

According to a regulatory filing, Berkshire bought about 924,000 Sirius XM shares between October 30 and November 3, lifting its holding to about 125.7 million shares. Most of the stake is held through insurer GEICO, with the rest in Berkshire subsidiary pension plans. Based on Sirius XM’s market value of about $11.2 billion, that equates to roughly 37% of the company.

The buying came at higher prices than Berkshire’s previous reported purchases. It paid an average of roughly $29 to $30 a share, compared with about $21 to $22 when it last added to the position in mid-2025, and it kept buying as the stock rose. Sirius XM shares have gained about 13% over the past week, closing at around $33 on Wednesday.

The purchases followed Sirius XM’s third-quarter results on October 29. Revenue was broadly flat and earnings came in slightly below forecasts, but the company raised its full-year guidance for a second consecutive quarter, reported a 14% rise in free cash flow and said it expects to step up share buybacks significantly in 2027. The risks have not gone away: listener numbers at its Pandora service fell, leverage is elevated and management expects a tougher fourth quarter for subscribers.

The wider market context gives the move added resonance. On Wednesday, US stocks rallied broadly while investors rotated out of AI infrastructure names, with the Dow surging about 1,570 points even as Nvidia and other chip stocks fell. Research houses including UBS have been urging investors to trim concentrated technology exposure, while others have warned that the AI spending cycle may be peaking.

Berkshire’s purchases predate that selloff, so they are not a reaction to it. But a bet on a mature, cash-rich business returning capital to shareholders sits squarely on the other side of the AI capex trade that has dominated markets this year.

Whether the rotation lasts will shape how much attention such value plays attract. For now, Berkshire’s willingness to pay up signals continued conviction in Sirius XM, even after a sharp rally. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.
